title: Beringian standstill
summary: Genetic and paleogenomic analyses indicate that ancestral Native Americans separated from East Asian populations roughly 25,000–20,000 years ago and experienced thousands of years of demographic isolation in Beringia before expanding into the Americas. During this standstill, unique founding mitochondrial and nuclear lineages differentiated, including the newly identified Ancient Beringians, while coalesced glacial ice sheets blocked southward dispersal until late Pleistocene deglaciation opened coastal and interior routes.
